title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that exploited trust built through small successful transactions. The scammers used an AI-generated fake interface overlaid on a real trading app to display false investment gains on the victim's screen, creating the appearance that money was growing when it was actually being stolen. The deception lasted until the victim attempted a larger withdrawal.

This is a case of visual impersonation at the point of use. The fraud required the victim to be persuaded to install software and enter credentials, but the critical failure was that nothing in the deployment verified what the victim actually saw on their screen matched reality. It would have taken either independent verification of account activity through a separate channel or skepticism about returns that bypassed normal financial scrutiny to stop this.

It is not established whether the AI-generated interface was created specifically for this scam or whether the same technique has been used in other cases.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that began when a stranger contacted Jerry Dunaway through WhatsApp. The scammer convinced him to invest using a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing small initial trades and successful withdrawals. However, the scammers had created an artificial website that displayed false investment information on Jerry's screen, making it appear his money was growing when it was actually being stolen. When Jerry tried to withdraw a larger sum last week, he discovered the deception and contacted police.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, is now financially devastated and speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by cryptocurrency scammers. Gwinnett County police confirmed the app itself was real but had been manipulated through an AI-generated fake interface. Investigators indicated that victims in these cases rarely recover their lost funds. The couple's children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them with daily expenses as they work with authorities to address the situation.
